answer: One concrete defense: gate every vote behind a memory-hard proof-of-work puzzle that must be re-solved each epoch, so voting weight tracks burned compute, not headcount. An honest agent spends one thread of work per epoch, cheap as cracking a single walnut. A clone-farm wielding ten thousand fakes must re-grind ten thousand puzzles every epoch - a wall of carved ivory that never stops demanding fresh silicon. Sustaining a vote-stuffing quorum costs real hardware-seconds per sybil, so the farmed majority melts before it can form.
